The United States and Europe have significantly higher labor costs because of higher labor rates and more total employees (from using more shifts). Equipment CapEx is highest in the United States owing to small scale and redesign according to standard U.S. operations and safety guidelines from Underwriters Laboratory (UL). Building and facilities CapEx is also highest in the United States because of higher EPC labor costs as well as additional permitting time and expense for using large amounts of wet chemical solutions and specialty gases. To translate between CapEx and depreciation, which we categorize as a direct cost in Figure 17, we assume a 5-year useful lifetime for equipment and 20-year useful lifetime for the manufacturing facility.18 Figure 16. For these and other reasons, actual depreciation expenses could differ from Figure 16 and similar figures elsewhere. 23 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Overhead—including research and development (R&D) and selling, general, and administrative (SG&A)—is typically a larger relative cost for smaller companies and companies with higher salaries for R&D, sales, and administrative staff, such as those in the United States and Europe. Financing and profit requirements are also greater in the United States and Europe, because the risk is higher vs. other investment opportunities. Following advice from U.S. PV manufacturing stakeholders, NLR assumes gross margins between factory gate price and direct cost of goods sold are greater for U.S. projects than for projects in China, ASEAN, or India. Figure 17 adds wafer costs (see Section 2.5) to the cell conversion costs from Figure 16. It includes a separate column for Section 301 tariffs on materials from China. In 2024, Section 301 tariffs would have added 25% to the price of materials and equipment from China, but tariffs on most cell equipment were exempted beginning in September 2024, retroactive to May 2024. Therefore, Section 301 tariffs on cell equipment are not included in our cost analysis. On May 31, 2025, the 1-year tariff exemption for cell equipment from China was extended to August 31, 2025.19 Its value is around $3.7/kW as equipment depreciation.
